citation.note: Written notice requirement: any change in pay rate, payday, or place of pay must be communicated in writing no later than the payday preceding the effective date of the change (AS § 23.05.160's "on the payday before the time of change").

Payroll record retention: employers must keep, at the employee's place of employment, each employee's name, address, occupation, rate of pay and amount paid each pay period, and hours worked each day and workweek, for at least 3 years (AS § 23.10.100).

Paid sick leave (Ballot Measure 1): employees accrue 1 hour per 30 hours worked, capped at 40 hours annually (employers < 15 FTE) or 56 hours (employers ≥15 FTE); full carryover; no payout on termination; rehire within 6 months restores the balance (AS §§ 23.10.066–.067).

body.interaction_rule: Paid sick leave (Ballot Measure 1): employees accrue 1 hour per 30 hours worked, capped at 40 hours annually (employers < 15 FTE) or 56 hours (employers ≥15 FTE); full carryover; no payout on termination; rehire within 6 months restores the balance (AS §§ 23.10.066–.067).

citation.note: Employers must pay employees at least semi-monthly; more frequent payment is permitted (AS § 23.05.140).

Final pay: all wages due within 3 working days of employer-initiated termination; within 3 days of the next regular payday if employee-initiated (minimum 3 days after notice received); late-payment penalty of regular wages up to 90 working days (AS § 23.05.140(f)–(g)).

body.deadline_description: Final pay: all wages due within 3 working days of employer-initiated termination; within 3 days of the next regular payday if employee-initiated (minimum 3 days after notice received); late-payment penalty of regular wages up to 90 working days (AS § 23.05.140(f)–(g)).

citation.note: Minimum wage $14.00/hour as of 2026-07-01, rising to $15.00/hour on 2027-07-01, then indexed annually to Anchorage CPI-U from 2028-01-01 with a $2.00/hour floor above federal. No tip credit (AS § 23.10.065).

Pay statement content and form: employers must provide written or electronic pay stubs (AS § 23.05.140(d)) showing straight-time and overtime hours, rates of pay, gross wages, itemized deductions, pay period dates, employer name and address, and current sick-leave balance.
Contractor classification test (ABC test): Alaska Statute § 23.20.525(a)(8)(A–C) applies the ABC test for unemployment-insurance and workers'-compensation purposes.

body.test_description: Contractor classification test (ABC test): Alaska Statute § 23.20.525(a)(8)(A–C) applies the ABC test for unemployment-insurance and workers'-compensation purposes.

citation.note: Employee access to personnel files: employees and former employees have a statutory right to inspect and copy their own personnel files during reasonable business hours under reasonable rules; employers may charge the reasonable actual cost of copying (AS § 23.10.430).
Captive audience ban (Ballot Measure 1): employers cannot require employees to attend meetings primarily about political or religious matters; retaliation for refusal is prohibited (AS § 23.10.135).

citation.note: Drug testing: No state statute regulating or restricting drug testing in private employment.

Data breach notification: entities collecting personal information must notify affected Alaska residents of a breach of unencrypted personal information in the most expeditious time possible and without unreasonable delay; 1,000+ residents triggers Alaska Attorney General notice (AS § 45.48.010).
